headline: Language model agents automate biomedical evidence classification and interpretation
label: Llm Agents For Biomedical Interpretation
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair LLM agents with retrieval and curated evidence for variant, phenotype, and single-cell data interpretation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is grounding language models in domain-specific evidence through retrieval, curated guidelines, databases, or specialized embeddings. A severity classifier combining ReAct and RAG reaches 93.55% accuracy on 10,211 HPO terms using ACMG/ACOG guidelines and PubMed, and HeartVar automates ACMG/AMP variant classification with rule-based queries of 20 databases. scACORN orchestrates specialized small language models for question answering over single-cell transcriptomic profiles, while Genolator fuses DNA, amino acid, and protein structure embeddings with natural language. Benchmarks quantify performance across this class: LongevityBench evaluates 18 AI systems on 17 aging biodata tasks, and a concept normalization study compares 15 biomedical transformers with 12 instruction-tuned LLMs, with SapBERT leading. BioPhys-Bridge targets interdisciplinary reasoning, so the shared claim is methodological rather than universal.
